citations.claim: energy just before ceiling bounce, still below limit
first energy_bound violation at ceiling bounce, energy exceeds allowed 1000.31
velocity after bounce shows speed increase (energy gain) despite e<1

counterfactual.change: changed bodies[0].e from 0.9978 to 0.2 (single field) to reduce restituted energy at bounce; this eliminates the spurious gain and energy stays below limit, proving high restitution bounce is causally required

explanation: Shrunk scenario has single fast body (speed ~41-42 m/s) with near-elastic restitution e=0.998 bouncing off ceiling. Energy is stable ~988 J for steps 50-62 (below 10%+5 J limit ~1000.3 J) but jumps to ~1003 J at step 63 after ceiling bounce, exceeding the limit despite e<1 should dissipate energy. Controller off, gravity 9.81, 5 substeps. Likely cause is collision response: impulse with high restitution plus positional correction for penetration adds spurious mechanical energy at high-speed impacts, exceeding the energy_bound tolerance. Lowering restitution removes the gain.
vision_note: Frames 60-62 show a single blue body near the top-edge (ceiling) in the upper-right, drifting upward just to the right of a thin vertical interior wall. Frame 63 shows it slightly lower after contacting the top boundary, indicating a near-elastic ceiling bounce with no obvious tunneling, penetration or large positional jump.
